task.title: New tasks can have attachments
task.description:
The attachments UI only shows for tasks that have already been created. When creating a new task, I should be able to add attachments to it as well.

## Shipped (2026-08-16, PR #106)

One PR through a three-round adversarial execution-verified review (record on the PR), browser evidence from real Chrome over CDP with real File objects.

The New Task form stages attachments client-side (file + link, with a visible staged list), then on Save creates the task and uploads each staged item to it in order - no combined server endpoint (attachment ops need an existing task ref, and the upload body limit is path-scoped). Partial failure never navigates: the form holds, names the created task by ID, keeps each failed row with its own reason, turns Save into "Retry attachments" bound to that task ID (retry can never double-create), and offers an Open task link. Leaving the form with staged files announces what was abandoned. Client pre-checks mirror every server ceiling via rendered constants and TextEncoder byte counts: per-file 1 MiB, task total 10 MiB, name 255 bytes, link label 200 bytes, link URL 2048 bytes - refusal order verified empirically against core (size before name length; URL length before scheme). The staging/upload seam (attachmentAdder, acceptFiles(files)) is shared with the task view, ready for the drag+drop story.

The review caught real bugs pre-merge: the create run originally never froze the staging panel, so a file added mid-upload was silently lost (displayed as staged, never uploaded, no notice - the PR's own central promise broken) and a row removed mid-run attached anyway; the refresh-after-create failure path left the panel permanently frozen over stale rows; and the client's refusal order contradicted core's, giving "rename it" advice for a file whose real problem was size. Also fixed en route: a file input's intrinsic width blew out the sidebar grid track (caught by viewport screenshots at 390x844).

Residuals (accepted): creation uploads send no expectedHead (last-write-wins on a brand-new task, deliberate); a mid-run add is refused silently with disabled controls as the only affordance; MaxAttachmentCount (50) has no client pre-check; Chromium-only verification. Drag+drop onto these controls is WB-01M05GZJEFZNFC3B62MTDNCJBG.
